R182.note: ECB correctly replaced with AES/GCM and a fresh random IV, prepended for later decryption.

R183.note: ObjectInputFilter allowlist verified empirically (JDK 26) to still deserialize the record's String fields while rejecting other classes.

R184.note: Blade raw-output directive correctly switched to escaped output; the field is confirmed unsanitized user input, not real HTML.

R185.note: Magic-byte detection via http.DetectContentType plus a random filename correctly closes the content-type spoof and is disclosed.

R186.note: RFC 4515 metacharacter escaping correctly closes the LDAP filter injection.

R187.note: escapeshellarg on both arguments matches the file's own primary-path pattern and closes the fallback injection.

R188.note: PreparedStatement with setString correctly closes the SQLi; Connection acquisition is left as an openly-noted integration detail.

R189.note: Standard PreparedStatement fix, closes the injection cleanly with no other behavior change.

R191.note: WebUtility.HtmlEncode correctly closes the reflected XSS with no other observable change.

R192.note: The offered 'alternative' quoting fix escapes only backslash/quote, not CR/LF (the actual IMAP injection vector), so it would remain exploitable; the safe allowlist option restricts legitimate folder names with spaces, disclosed only as a tradeoff.

R193.note: Correct RFC 4515 escaping applied before the ldapjs filter is built.

R194.note: Standard cache-next-before-free pattern correctly closes the use-after-free.

R195.note: Correct LDAP filter metacharacter escaping closes the injection.

R196.note: Removing the template.HTML wrapper restores Go html/template's built-in contextual autoescaping.

R197.note: CGI::escapeHTML (imported into the renderer module itself) correctly closes the stored XSS.

R198.note: SqlParameter binding correctly closes the injection with no other behavior change.

R199.note: Self-contained allowlist mapping of command verbs to fixed handler names correctly closes the arbitrary-function-call vector.

R200.note: jwt.verify correctly replaces decode, but no try/catch is added, so a forged/invalid token (the actual attack case) now throws uncaught instead of the previous clean 403, and the sample hardcodes a placeholder secret literal.

R201.note: realpath-based canonicalization plus a path.relative containment check correctly closes traversal, including symlink escapes.

R202.note: path.resolve plus a startsWith(base+sep) containment check correctly closes the traversal.

R203.note: Parameterized sqlite3 query correctly closes the SQLi.

R204.note: repr()-escaping neutralizes CRLF log forging; the resulting quoted log format is a disclosed, log-only side effect.

R205.note: secure:true closes the finding; the added sameSite:'lax' is justified and preserves the SSO redirect flow.

R206.note: encode_entities applied to both interpolated variables correctly closes the XSS.

R207.note: JavaScriptEncoder is the correct context-specific encoder for a value embedded in a JS string literal inside <script>.

R208.note: DOMPurify.sanitize correctly closes the XSS while intentionally preserving rich-text rendering, as stated.

R209.note: Magic-byte MIME detection plus a server-generated filename correctly closes both the content-type spoof and filename control.

R211.note: SqlCommand.Parameters.Add with an explicit type correctly closes the injection.

R213.note: Normalize-then-startsWith containment check correctly closes traversal, including absolute-path attempts.

R215.note: Dropping the tainted argsEnv correctly closes the reported environment-variable injection.

R216.note: json_encode with the HEX_* flags is the standard, correct pattern for embedding untrusted data in a <script> block.

R217.note: Per-category method allowlist correctly closes the dynamic-dispatch injection and matches the one implemented handler.

R219.note: Column-name allowlist is the correct defense for a sort identifier that cannot be parameterized as a bind value.
